explanation: The revolution’s own article says what it was made of: “The revolution was the culmination of a decade of agitation, revolts, and uprisings.” The Second Guangzhou Uprising — Huang Xing’s failed rising at Canton in April 1911, six months before Wuchang — is one of those revolts, and Wikidata’s item says so too. **Neither article names this uprising as a cause of the revolution**, and the edge is written at the strength that supports: `precondition-of`, `probable`, and not `caused`.
